title: As an IT admin, the SSO catalog covers my stack — thousands of pre-built SAML/OIDC app integrations that connect in minutes, not custom projects
As an IT admin, apps outside the catalog still get SSO — custom SAML, OIDC, and header-based apps configured with documented walkthroughs
As an employee, one portal holds my work apps — a launcher dashboard (and browser extension) where I sign in once and reach everything I'm assigned
As an IT admin, accounts create themselves — SCIM provisioning pushes users, groups, and entitlements into downstream apps the moment access is assigned
As a security engineer, offboarding is one action — deactivating a user kills their sessions and deprovisions their accounts across connected apps immediately
As an IT admin, HR drives identity — the HRIS is the source of truth, and joiner/mover/leaver changes flow into the directory and app assignments automatically
As a security engineer, MFA goes beyond push codes — FIDO2 security keys and passkeys are supported and can be REQUIRED by policy for sensitive apps
As a security engineer, access decisions weigh context — network, device, location, and risk signals drive conditional policies per app and group
As an employee, I can sign in without a password — passwordless flows via passkeys, authenticator, or platform biometrics documented and supported
As a security engineer, only healthy devices get in — device posture (managed, encrypted, screen-locked) is checked in the auth policy before an app session is granted
As an IT admin, devices are managed from the same platform or a documented MDM integration — enrollment, policy enforcement, and remote lock/wipe tied to identity
As a developer, the directory is fully programmable — documented REST APIs for users, groups, and app assignments with pagination, filtering, and clear auth
As an IT admin, access is assigned by group and rule — dynamic group membership and group-based app assignment replace one-by-one grants
As an IT admin, legacy protocols still work — cloud LDAP and RADIUS endpoints serve the VPNs, Wi-Fi, and older systems that will never speak SAML
As an IT admin, identity events trigger automation — no-code workflows on hire, role change, and departure handle the app-by-app choreography for me
As a security engineer, access gets re-justified on a schedule — certification campaigns route who-has-what to reviewers and produce audit-ready sign-off records
As a platform engineer, the IdP is managed as code — an official Terraform provider (or equivalent) covers apps, groups, and policies so identity config is reviewable and reproducible
As a security engineer, every identity event is queryable and exportable — a structured system log with API access and native streaming to my SIEM
As a developer, I can subscribe to identity events — webhooks/event hooks fire on user lifecycle and auth events so downstream systems react in real time
As a security engineer, I can judge the vendor's own record — published security incident postmortems, a live trust page, and honest disclosure history
As an AI-native team, AI agents are first-class identities — documented patterns for securing agent access to apps (cross-app access, token vaulting, scoped agent credentials)
